title: Banned internal identifiers
description: Every internal identifier this project uses, parsed from the registries that define them by scripts/build_catalogue.py. DECISIONS.md D-05: the ban is mechanical, and the list is generated because a hand-kept one goes stale on the first identifier somebody adds. Consumed by the terminology gate, which packet P2 owns. Two exemptions that gate must carry: this file itself, and the routes where a frozen record's own identifier is the content rather than jargon standing in for prose.

total.description: A floor and not a target: the list can only be complete or short, and short is a gate that passes on text it should have caught. LOWERED FROM 600 AT BUILD TIME, and the reason is a correction rather than a relaxation. The generator was adding all 190 quantity ids and all 17 refusal reason names, neither of which is in DECISIONS.md D-05's family table, and both of which are PUBLIC VOCABULARY this site prints on purpose: /atlas/ is a catalogue of quantities and /docs/refusals/ is the page about those seventeen, so banning them banned two routes outright. Removing them takes the count from 606 to 399. The old floor was set from D-05's estimate of roughly 620, which GROUND-TRUTH.md C-31 had already shown does not reproduce from the registries D-05 names.

families.description: Keyed by family so a gate failure can name the registry the term came from, which is the difference between a useful message and 'banned term found'.

terms.description: The flat union, sorted. This is what the gate matches against.
